Thanks again for taking the time this morning — good discussion. Per our demo and discovery, below is a concise recap + network items we need to qualify so we can scope a Private VPC (or confirm if Dedicated is a better fit). I put owners for each ask so nothing slips.

Summary of preferred deployment modes you mentioned:
- Private VPC (preferred for compliance) — primary path to scope
- Dedicated capacity (fallback if network constraints)
- Hosted API (not an option for regulated workloads right now)

Network / connectivity items to confirm (action items):
1) PrivateLink vs VPC peering: Elena/Tom — do you have a preference or restriction? If none, we typically recommend PrivateLink for cross-account isolation and fewer route table changes (owner: Finovate).
2) Egress allowlist: Finovate to confirm whether you require a static egress IP from Redwood, or if egress will be NAT'ed through your own egress and we should expect customer-supplied IPs. If you need Redwood-supplied IPs, we will provide 2-3 stable IPv4 addresses for allowlisting (owner: Redwood - Karthik).
3) Required outbound ports: our baseline is 443/TLS to support model traffic and health checks; if you have proxy or firewall appliances that inspect TLS, please list interception ports (owner: Finovate).
4) DNS & TLS: If using PrivateLink we provide internal endpoint DNS names; if you require custom certs, share ACM / certificate manager details (owner: Finovate).
5) Network preflight: please complete the attached Finovate_network_matrix.xlsx with VPC IDs, route table IDs, and security groups so we can validate (owner: Finovate).

Next steps and timeline:
- Today: Finovate to return network matrix + preference on PrivateLink vs peering (ETA: Tue 5/18)
- Wed 5/19: Karthik will validate details and return a preflight checklist and proposed egress IPs
- Fri 5/21: tentative kick-off for Private VPC provisioning once preflight clears

Attachments: redwood_vpc_preflight_checklist.pdf (checklist we’ll use), Finovate_network_matrix.xlsx (your input).

If it's helpful I can loop in our engagement manager to draft a mutual action plan and tentative dates for PO/contract steps.

Thanks — Lauren

Thanks, Lauren — helpful recap. Short answers inline: 

1) PrivateLink vs peering: prefer PrivateLink for least blast radius. We have existing peering rules but PrivateLink keeps auditors happier.
2) Egress allowlist: we prefer Redwood to provide static egress IPs that we can allowlist on outbound (customer egress flows through our NAT gateway). We'll need 2 failover IPs if possible.
3) Ports: we can open outbound 443 and 9443 if needed (our security team inspects TLS).
4) DNS/certs: we will accept your internal endpoint DNS. No custom certs required on our side.
5) Network matrix: attaching initial completed sheet; will follow up with VPC IDs tomorrow after networking sync.

Also attaching Finovate_compliance_matrix.xlsx — highlights a few additional audit asks (data residency notes). We are aiming for a June window for production, ideally mid-June.

Subject: Re: Private VPC implementation scope and egress IPs — technical notes and sample allowlist

Elena — thanks for the quick turnaround and the matrix. Quick technical responses to help your networking team plan: 

PrivateLink vs peering
- PrivateLink (AWS VPC Endpoint) is our recommended path for cross-account private connectivity: it keeps traffic on the AWS backbone and minimizes route table changes on your primary compute subnets. We will provision an interface endpoint in your account via endpoint service.

Health checks / routing
- No peering route table entries are required for PrivateLink itself. You will see ENIs in the VPC and we will request that you allow inbound connections from the endpoint ENI to the service port. Our health checks will use source IPs from the private endpoint ENIs — no public IPs.

Egress / allowlist options
- Option A (recommended for your auditors): Redwood supplies two stable IPv4 egress addresses for outbound model calls originating from our managed control-plane (used for callbacks, billing webhooks, etc.). Example (reserved-test): 198.51.100.21 and 198.51.100.22 — please add to your firewall allowlist.
- Option B: All egress flows route through your NAT; in this case you only need to accept PrivateLink traffic and we won't provide public egress IPs.

Ports & TLS
- Primary: 443 (TLS). We also use 8443 for internal admin endpoints when working with diagnostics (we can disable if you prefer).

Network preflight deliverable (attached): redwood_vpc_preflight_checklist.pdf — contains steps we will run during validation.

Action items (Karthik / Redwood):
- I will send a formal preflight report with the two egress IPs and a minimal ruleset template by Wed 5/19.
- Marissa will be your provisioning lead for scheduling the endpoint creation and validation (cc'd).

If it's helpful, we can run a 30-minute call with your network ops on Tue 5/18 to walk the preflight steps.

-Karthik
